page: Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 4245P processor built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 3.8 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. System memory consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, which provides 2.67 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and comprises a 1920 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is present on this server configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate exceptional single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scoring, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. It also registers top-tier performance in image and text processing, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU score, falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth reads are average, though large-block memory write bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%. For lightweight AI tasks, the server delivers top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M LLM models, though performance scales down to average for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal instance provides dedicated, non-virtualized hardware resources and high-capacity local NVMe storage without the overhead of a hypervisor. The high single-core clock speed of 3.8 GHz and strong single-threaded performance make it highly suitable for workloads that do not scale infinitely across threads but require rapid sequential processing. Recommended workloads include single-threaded or lightly threaded applications, software compilation, text and image processing pipelines, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from fast local NVMe storage.
